question: A factory sensor flags machines likely to fail this week. Failures are rare; the sensor is usually right. Most flags turn out to be nothing. Is the sensor broken?
options: No, that is what a rare event looks like
answer: When the thing being looked for almost never happens, even a good detector produces mostly false alarms — there is simply far more of everything else. The number worth watching is how many real failures it misses, not how many alarms are quiet.
move: Judge a detector by what it misses, not by how often it cries wolf.
trap: Judging a detector by how often its alarms are real.
source: Precision and recall on rare events
reference: Saito & Rehmsmeier, The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets, PLOS ONE, 2015
